component_description: Consider the various degrees of human oversight in the decision-making process: a. Human-in-the-Loop: This model suggests that human oversight is active and involved, with the human retaining full control and the AI only providing recommendations or input. Decisions cannot be exercised without affirmative actions by the human, such as a human command to proceed with a given decision. (NB: Considering here also the concept of “Human in the Loophole” where there is automation bias, anchoring or confirmation bias in respect of the human operative. The human essentially affirming the AI outcome without critically assessing whether it is correct or not.) b. Human-out-of-the-Loop: This model suggests that there is no human oversight over the execution of decisions. AI has full control without the option of human override. c. Human-over-the-Loop: This model allows humans to adjust parameters during the execution of the algorithm.1

component_description: Consider minimizing inherent bias: • Selection Bias: This bias occurs when the data used to produce the AI System are not fully representative of the actual data or environment that the AI System may receive or function in. Common examples of selection bias in datasets are omission bias and stereotype bias. • Measurement Bias: This bias occurs when the data collection device causes the data to be systematically skewed in a particular direction. • Weighting Bias: This bias occurs when the data used by the AI Solution are attributed differing weights in producing the relevant outcome. The datasets might be afforded greater or lesser value, which might be arbitrarily or inaccurately awarded. • The following factors should be assessed (amongst others): – the frequency with which the dataset is reviewed and updated; – representativeness of the dataset to the end-user demographic and desired outcomes; – the diversity of the dataset, and the variety of sources from which the data has been collected (i.e. numeric, text, audio, visual, transactional, etc.); and – the usability of different datasets, including how those datasets have been matched and cleaned so that relational datasets can be correlated and linked.
llm_verbatim_span: Consider minimizing inherent bias: • Selection Bias: This bias occurs when the data used to produce the AI System are not fully representative of the actual data or environment that the AI System may receive or function in. llm_justification: This component explicitly addresses preventing systematic errors that discriminate (selection bias, stereotype bias, measurement bias, weighting bias) and requires assessing dataset representativeness to end-user demographics, which is the core concern of Avoidance of Unfair Bias (12), not merely data quality for accuracy (5) or data management compliance (8).

llm_justification: This component concerns intellectual property and open-source licensing decisions, which are not addressed by any of the 27 sub-principles; it is neither a transparency/auditability requirement (which focus on documentation and evaluation capability) nor a compliance obligation covered by the codebook.

component_description: Can the right to object to the processing of one's data be easily exercised by the individual for both the training and production phases? Can individuals exercise this right at any time (before and after the data is collected)?
llm_verbatim_span: Can the right to object to the processing of one's data be easily exercised by the individual for both the training and production phases? Can individuals exercise this right at any time (before and after the data is collected)?
llm_justification: This component explicitly asks about the implementation of a data-subject right (right to object to processing) across the AI lifecycle, which is a core data protection compliance mechanism covered by Data Governance (8), not a broader privacy-impact assessment (7) or a traceability/logging question (9).

component_description: Accountability and Privacy
llm_verbatim_span: Accountability and Privacy
llm_justification: This is a short heading naming two topics; Privacy (code 7) is chosen as the primary code because it represents a specific substantive right/impact concern, whereas Accountability encompasses multiple sub-principles (18, 19) and the label does not specify which aspect, making Privacy the more determinate single best fit.

component_description: Organisations can consider disclosing the manner in which an AI decision may affect an individual consumer, and whether the decision is reversible.
llm_verbatim_span: disclosing the manner in which an AI decision may affect an individual consumer, and whether the decision is reversible
llm_justification: This is Communication (11) rather than Explainability (10) because it focuses on conveying system capabilities, limitations, and decision consequences to users—specifically how decisions affect individuals and reversibility—rather than explaining the technical reasoning process of how the AI reaches its conclusions.

component_description: Are measures in place to ensure the integrity, robustness, and overall security of the AI system / application against potential attacks over its life cycle?
llm_verbatim_span: ensure the integrity, robustness, and overall security of the AI system / application against potential attacks over its life cycle
llm_justification: The component specifically names security and protection against attacks as its dominant concern, which directly maps to Resilience to Attack and Security (3) rather than General Safety (4) which focuses on safety hazards and harm, or Risk Management (19) which concerns governance processes.

component_description: 13. How is the enterprise's use/development of AI classified under the AI Act, and what requirements apply to the services used/developed?
llm_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)
llm_verbatim_span: How is the enterprise's use/development of AI classified under the AI Act, and what requirements apply to the services used/developed?
llm_justification: This component explicitly asks about legal classification under the AI Act and applicable legal requirements, which is the core definition of Compliance and Legal (21) - mapping applicable obligations from sectoral/product safety regimes with accountable owners - rather than general risk management (19) or data-protection-specific compliance (8).

component_description: If a bias has been identified, what steps have been taken to reduce it?
llm_verbatim_span: what steps have been taken to reduce it?
llm_justification: This is Avoidance of Unfair Bias (12) rather than Risk Management (19) because it specifically concerns bias mitigation measures—a core fairness concern—not the broader risk governance process.

component_description: What measures do you implement to ensure the cyber-security of the AI system?
llm_verbatim_span: What measures do you implement to ensure the cyber-security of the AI system?
llm_justification: The component explicitly asks about cyber-security measures, which directly maps to Resilience to Attack and Security (3) that assesses vulnerability to cyber threats and protective measures, rather than General Safety (4) which focuses on safety hazards/harm or Risk Management (19) which concerns broader governance processes.

component_description: Is the AI System following a deterministic approach as opposed to a probabilistic model?
llm_verbatim_span: Is the AI System following a deterministic approach as opposed to a probabilistic model?
llm_justification: This question concerns whether the system produces consistent, reproducible outputs (deterministic) versus variable outputs (probabilistic), which is the core concern of Reliability, Fall-back and Reproducibility (6) - evaluating consistent performance and reproducibility - rather than Accuracy (5) which focuses on precision/correctness of outputs.

component_description: Have cases of error been investigated?
llm_verbatim_span: Have cases of error been investigated?
llm_justification: This is about investigating errors to understand system reliability and prevent recurrence, which is central to Reliability, Fall-back and Reproducibility (6) rather than General Safety (4) which focuses on initial hazard identification, or Performance and Monitoring (23) which emphasizes ongoing operational surveillance with thresholds.

component_description: Based upon the gravity and effort to overcome prejudice create the severity table
llm_verbatim_span: Based upon the gravity and effort to overcome prejudice create the severity table
llm_justification: The component requires creating a severity classification for prejudice based on its gravity and remediation effort, which is a bias detection and assessment mechanism rather than a design accessibility concern (13) or general risk management (19).

component_description: Have appropriate technical and organizational measures and criteria been defined to storage personal data?
llm_verbatim_span: appropriate technical and organizational measures and criteria been defined to storage personal data
llm_justification: This is Data Governance (8) rather than Privacy (7) because it asks about specific data-management compliance practices (technical and organizational measures for storing personal data), not about rights/risk impact on data subjects; it is also not Traceability (9) because it concerns storage measures/criteria, not provenance or logging of which data produced outputs.

component_description: Investigate the model accuracy
llm_verbatim_span: Investigate the model accuracy
llm_justification: This is a direct requirement to examine model accuracy (code 5), not a broader performance monitoring process (23), reliability assessment (6), or general safety evaluation (4).

llm_verbatim_span: Requires regular, independent third-party audits to verify compliance with the AIC4 framework.
llm_justification: The dominant requirement is enabling independent evaluation of the AI system through third-party audits, which directly maps to Auditability (18) rather than Risk Management (19) which would focus on the risk-identification/mitigation process itself.

component_description: Is this information publicly available?
llm_verbatim_span: Is this information publicly available?
llm_justification: This question asks about public availability of information, which directly supports auditability by enabling independent evaluation and external scrutiny, rather than internal traceability (9) or user-facing communication (11).

component_description: Risk Notifications: Agencies must inform the Digital Transformation Agency (DTA) of high-risk AI use cases and apply a risk assessment framework (outlined in Attachment B).
llm_verbatim_span: Agencies must inform the Digital Transformation Agency (DTA) of high-risk AI use cases and apply a risk assessment framework
llm_justification: The dominant requirement is the governance process for identifying and reporting risks to an external oversight body (DTA) and applying a risk assessment framework, which is the core of Risk Management (19), not the technical capability to be audited (18) or a specific safety hazard assessment (4).

component_description: Embed new Responsible AI-specific roles and reskilling programs across the organization.

component_description: Does the training data include data related to the particular characteristics of the individuals such as their gender, age, physical characteristics, sensitive data, etc.? Which characteristics?
llm_verbatim_span: Does the training data include data related to the particular characteristics of the individuals such as their gender, age, physical characteristics, sensitive data, etc.?

component_description: Is the AI System periodically audited or assessed with respect to transparency and explainability, either internally or by an independent third party?
llm_verbatim_span: Is the AI System periodically audited or assessed with respect to transparency and explainability, either internally or by an independent third party?
llm_justification: This asks about the capability for independent evaluation of the AI system (specifically its transparency/explainability), which is the core definition of Auditability (18), not the transparency mechanisms themselves (9-11) nor the audit's own scoping (25).

component_description: Controller/processor dynamics in AI supply chains.

llm_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)
llm_verbatim_span: Controller/processor dynamics in AI supply chains.

component_description: Your organisation uses for its own account, provides to its customers or operates on behalf of its customers applications based on AI models with which users can interact. What measure does it implement to inform users?
llm_verbatim_span: What measure does it implement to inform users?

llm_verbatim_span: Not only is checking on data itself relevant, but also so-called proxies, model bias, and so on
llm_justification: This component specifically requires checking for bias through protected characteristics, proxies, and model bias—all core elements of detecting and preventing unfair bias (code 12)—rather than addressing accessibility/design barriers (code 13) or data quality for accuracy purposes (code 5).

component_description: Are there procedures to verify storage periods, criteria and implemented measures?
llm_verbatim_span: procedures to verify storage periods, criteria and implemented measures
llm_justification: This directly concerns data retention policies and verification of data management practices, which are central compliance mechanisms under Data Governance (8), rather than traceability of system outputs (9) or privacy impact assessment (7).

component_description: Review monitoring plans and documents that outline the scope and methods for continuous AI system evaluation.
llm_verbatim_span: monitoring plans and documents that outline the scope and methods for continuous AI system evaluation
llm_justification: This is Performance and Monitoring (23) rather than Reliability (6) because it explicitly requires reviewing plans for "continuous" evaluation with defined "scope and methods," which are the operational surveillance mechanisms that distinguish code 23 from capability-focused code 6.

llm_verbatim_span: limiting the AI's autonomy in specific high-risk situations

component_description: The relevance of the dataset and the context for data collection, as it may affect the interpretation of and reliance on the data for the intended purpose;

llm_verbatim_span: Have we identified all the important stakeholders needed in this phase of the project?

llm_verbatim_span: Simulates attacks like data poisoning to evaluate the vulnerability of the learning pipeline.
llm_justification: The component explicitly names a specific security attack pattern (data poisoning) and evaluates vulnerability to adversarial attacks on the learning pipeline, which directly maps to Resilience to Attack and Security rather than general safety hazards or broader risk management processes.

llm_verbatim_span: black-box testing considered as part of the testing plan in order to ensure that functionality of AI-based component is guaranteed, it behaves as expected and the information integrity is preserved
llm_justification: This is about verification/validation methods (black-box testing) to ensure consistent, expected performance and information integrity, which are core to Reliability, Fall-back and Reproducibility (6) rather than Accuracy (5) which focuses on prediction precision, or System Design (22) which concerns pre-deployment engineering processes.

component_description: Configuration management
llm_verbatim_span: Configuration management

component_description: Does the organization use strategic risk assessment techniques like scenario planning and assumptions testing for AI programs?
llm_verbatim_span: Does the organization use strategic risk assessment techniques like scenario planning and assumptions testing for AI programs?
llm_justification: This is Risk Management (19) rather than General Safety (4) because it concerns the broader governance process for risk assessment (scenario planning, assumptions testing) at the organizational/program level, not specific safety hazards or consequences of failure in a particular system.

llm_verbatim_span: Generate a set of both rational and irrational counterfactuals and determine their impact on outcomes.

component_description: Develop a portfolio view of risks and opportunities for AI initiatives
llm_verbatim_span: Develop a portfolio view of risks and opportunities for AI initiatives
llm_justification: This is Risk Management (19) rather than Organisational Context (20) because the dominant requirement is establishing a process for identifying and documenting risks across initiatives (a risk-governance mechanism), not merely linking individual systems to business purpose or strategy.

component_description: Compare results from observational and intervention phases.

llm_verbatim_span: Have developmental and operational policies procedures and controls been implemented pursuant to such methodology?

llm_verbatim_span: Document what processes and metrics will be used to evaluate whether production data (i.e., input data the system encounters during deployment) differs materially from training data.

llm_verbatim_span: Create an audit trail as to have failures be rigorously examined and accountability be asigned

llm_verbatim_span: Is the system being evaluated on ongoing basis and tested for performance, accuracy, unintended consequences, fairness?

component_description: Consideration of necessity, proportionality, and risk mitigation.
llm_verbatim_span: Consideration of necessity, proportionality, and risk mitigation.

llm_verbatim_span: How does the entity assess and mitigate biases in training and operational data?

component_description: transparency
llm_verbatim_span: transparency

component_description: Where an organisation has weighed the factors above and decided not to provide an option to opt out, it is prudent for the organisation to consider providing modes of recourse to the consumer such as providing a channel for reviewing the decision.

component_description: Analyze the business context

llm_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)

llm_verbatim_span: Are end-users informed of the duration of security coverage and updates? What length is the expected timeframe within which security updates for the AI system/application will be provided?

llm_verbatim_span: AI must comply with data privacy laws, particularly in handling personal data. This involves respecting the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) principles.
llm_justification: The component's dominant requirement is data protection COMPLIANCE practice (GDPR adherence), not privacy rights impact assessment (code 7) or technical traceability of data flows (code 9), making Data Governance (8) the best fit.

llm_verbatim_span: Counterfactual fairness testing ensures that a model's decisions are the same in both the real world and in a counterfactual world where attributes deemed sensitive (such as race or gender) are altered

component_description: For the definition of decision thresholds for models or automatic systems based on them, your organisation:
llm_verbatim_span: definition of decision thresholds for models or automatic systems based on them
llm_justification: Decision thresholds determine when a model's output triggers an action or decision, which is a core aspect of ensuring reliable and consistent performance across conditions, including handling of low-confidence outputs—the defining concern of Reliability, Fall-back and Reproducibility rather than general accuracy measurement or post-deployment monitoring.

component_description: Is the DPO assisted and advised by experts on specific matters relating to the AI component?
llm_verbatim_span: Is the DPO assisted and advised by experts on specific matters relating to the AI component?

component_description: RS18 - Discrimination risks: AI exhibiting bias or discrimination across demographic lines.
llm_verbatim_span: AI exhibiting bias or discrimination across demographic lines
llm_justification: This is Avoidance of Unfair Bias (12) rather than Accessibility (13) because it concerns discriminatory outcomes/decisions produced by the system across demographic groups, not design/interface barriers to access.

component_description: Is white-box testing at code and implementation levels included in the testing plan?
llm_verbatim_span: white-box testing at code and implementation levels included in the testing plan
llm_justification: White-box testing at code/implementation levels is a structured engineering practice and design-time verification method that reduces defects before deployment, which is the core focus of System Design and Development (22), rather than post-deployment monitoring (23) or outcome metrics like Reliability (6).

component_description: Identify Functions: Break down the system into smaller components or functions (e.g., data ingestion, model inference, output generation).
llm_verbatim_span: Break down the system into smaller components or functions (e.g., data ingestion, model inference, output generation)

component_description: Document rationale for choices made during the feature selection and engineering processes and evaluate their impact on model performance.
llm_verbatim_span: Document rationale for choices made during the feature selection and engineering processes
llm_justification: This is Traceability (9) rather than Explainability (10) because it focuses on documenting the development process and design decisions (which features were chosen and why), not on explaining the reasoning behind individual model outputs to end users.

component_description: Review the audit results
llm_verbatim_span: Review the audit results
llm_justification: This is coded as Auditability (18) rather than Risk Management (19) or Auditing Context (25) because it concerns the evaluation of audit outputs as part of enabling independent evaluation of the AI system, which is the core of auditability; it is not about the audit's scoping (25) nor the broader risk-management cycle (19).

component_description: Have the performance values between different options of AI components been compared in the context of a process of selection of the most appropriate component for a specific processing?

llm_verbatim_span: selection of the most appropriate component for a specific processing

component_description: Are they informed of how these rights can be exercised and with whom?

component_description: Keeping a register according to GDPR
llm_verbatim_span: Keeping a register according to GDPR

component_description: White-box: Full access to all model information.
llm_verbatim_span: Full access to all model information.
llm_justification: This describes a white-box audit scenario where complete model information is available for independent evaluation, which is the core concern of Auditability (18) rather than Traceability (9) which focuses on logging/tracking development processes, or Explainability (10) which concerns human-understandable reasoning.

llm_verbatim_span: What drove initial model choices (e.g., criterion, predictor set, algorithm)? Were they informed by theory or empirically derived? If empirically derived, from what data (and of what quality were those data)?

llm_verbatim_span: maintain a current and up to date log detailing all of the changes made to the model and the system

llm_verbatim_span: How long will impacts from the decision last?

llm_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)
llm_verbatim_span: Support players in the private sector with securing trust for AI
llm_justification: This is a strategic objective about fostering AI adoption and trust in the private sector, which aligns with Organisational Context and Strategy (20) rather than generic Risk Management (19) or Accountability mechanisms (18), as it concerns the broader purpose and alignment of AI within an organisational/sectoral context.

component_description: Does the Organisation foster open access to its privately held datasets? If so, is it clear who can access the datasets, for what purposes the datasets can be used and whether there will be any remuneration for granting access?
llm_verbatim_span: Does the Organisation foster open access to its privately held datasets? If so, is it clear who can access the datasets, for what purposes the datasets can be used
llm_justification: This is Data Governance (8) rather than Traceability (9) because it concerns data management practices—specifically access policies, permitted purposes, and usage conditions for datasets—which are core data governance compliance and policy questions, not technical provenance tracking.

component_description: Are all possible risks assesed and the harms the system could have classified (e.g. life and health, violation of rights etc.)?
llm_verbatim_span: Are all possible risks assesed and the harms the system could have classified (e.g. life and health, violation of rights etc.)?
llm_justification: This is Risk Management (19) rather than General Safety (4) because it asks about the broader governance PROCESS of identifying and documenting adverse impacts across multiple harm categories (life, health, rights violations), not just safety-specific hazards; the breadth of harm types and the emphasis on comprehensive assessment points to the risk-management framework.

component_description: Collect sao:InformationElement. Describes specific data points within a realized output.
llm_verbatim_span: Describes specific data points within a realized output.
llm_justification: This is Traceability (9) rather than Explainability (10) because it focuses on technically identifying and documenting which specific data points constitute an output, not on explaining the reasoning behind why that output was produced.

component_description: Ethics and non-maleficence Within your organisation:
human_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)
llm_verbatim_span: Ethics and non-maleficence
llm_justification: This heading signals ethical oversight and harm prevention, which maps to Risk Management's ethics review and adverse-impact minimisation processes, rather than any narrower technical or transparency principle.

component_description: Report on risk, culture and performance
llm_verbatim_span: Report on risk, culture and performance
llm_justification: The requirement to report on risk, culture and performance is a governance oversight mechanism characteristic of Risk Management (19) rather than Performance Monitoring (23), which focuses on operational KPIs and technical drift detection in deployed systems.

component_description: Do you have a multidisciplinary risk management team that can help with AI model risk mitigation planning?
llm_verbatim_span: multidisciplinary risk management team that can help with AI model risk mitigation planning
llm_justification: This asks about establishing a team/process for risk identification and mitigation planning, which is the core governance structure described in Risk Management (19), rather than a specific safety hazard (4), human oversight mechanism (2), or audit capability (18).

component_description: Has a dimension reduction been carried out in order to achieve a balance between complexity and generalization?
llm_verbatim_span: Has a dimension reduction been carried out in order to achieve a balance between complexity and generalization?
llm_justification: This asks about dimension reduction to balance complexity and generalization, which is a technique to ensure consistent, reliable performance across contexts—the core concern of Reliability, Fall-back and Reproducibility (6)—rather than a design-process control (22) or a post-deployment monitoring practice (23).

component_description: Verifiy the design of SAO and RAInS using automated tools
llm_verbatim_span: Verifiy the design of SAO and RAInS using automated tools
llm_justification: This is System Design and Development (22) rather than Reliability (6) or Auditability (18) because it specifically concerns verification of the design itself using automated tools as a process control, not outcome metrics or independent evaluation capability.

component_description: Create a risk assesment summary
llm_verbatim_span: Create a risk assesment summary
llm_justification: This is a requirement to produce a risk assessment summary, which is a core risk management documentation activity (code 19), not a specific safety hazard identification (code 4) or audit scoping exercise (code 25).

component_description: Has the organisation's compliance with personal and confidential data requirements been audited and is it recognised by a certification, label or equivalent?
llm_verbatim_span: compliance with personal and confidential data requirements been audited and is it recognised by a certification, label or equivalent
llm_justification: This is Data Governance (8) rather than Auditability (18) because the dominant requirement is about data protection COMPLIANCE mechanisms (audit and certification of personal/confidential data handling), not the broader capability of the AI system itself to be audited.

component_description: Are we preventing Data Leakage?
llm_verbatim_span: Are we preventing Data Leakage?
llm_justification: Data leakage is a specific security vulnerability concern about unauthorized data exposure or disclosure, which fits Resilience to Attack and Security rather than Data Governance (which focuses on compliance practices like DPIAs and retention) or Privacy (which focuses on rights/risk impact on data subjects).

component_description: Who has access to the AI System and the AI application?
llm_verbatim_span: Who has access to the AI System and the AI application?
llm_justification: This question directly concerns access control and authorization, which is a security matter about preventing unauthorized access to the system, making it a Resilience to Attack and Security issue rather than Data Governance (which would focus on data-subject rights and compliance) or other principles.

component_description: Reliability: Assesses whether the AI system consistently performs as expected under various conditions.
llm_verbatim_span: consistently performs as expected under various conditions
llm_justification: Code 6 (Reliability, Fall-back and Reproducibility) is the best fit because it explicitly covers 'consistent performance across contexts and conditions,' which directly matches the component's focus on consistent performance under various conditions, rather than accuracy of outputs (5) or general safety hazards (4).

component_description: Define the inputs and conditions leading to algorithmic decisions (antecedents).
llm_verbatim_span: Define the inputs and conditions leading to algorithmic decisions (antecedents).
llm_justification: This is Traceability (9) rather than Explainability (10) because it focuses on technically identifying and documenting WHICH inputs and conditions produced a decision, not on conveying human-understandable reasoning for WHY that decision was reached.

component_description: Are there measures adopted to ensure component independence?
llm_verbatim_span: measures adopted to ensure component independence
llm_justification: Component independence is a reliability and fault-tolerance concern (preventing cascading failures, ensuring consistent performance), which is the core focus of code 6, rather than a design process (22) or security/attack concern (3).

component_description: AI system is evaluated regularly for safety. Deployed product is demonstrated to be safe and can fail safely and gracefully if it is made to operate beyond its knowledge limits. Safety metrics implicate system reliability and robustness, real-time monitoring, and response times for AI system failures.
llm_verbatim_span: AI system is evaluated regularly for safety. Deployed product is demonstrated to be safe and can fail safely and gracefully if it is made to operate beyond its knowledge limits. Safety metrics implicate system reliability and robustness, real-time monitoring, and response times for AI system failures.
llm_justification: The component's dominant requirement is ongoing post-deployment surveillance with safety metrics, real-time monitoring, and response protocols for failures in live context, which distinguishes it from General Safety (4) that focuses on pre-deployment hazard identification, and from Reliability/Fall-back (6) that concerns capability rather than operational thresholds and intervention procedures.

component_description: Introduce controlled modifications to the algorithm (e.g., swapping ads between users or changing content delivery methods).
llm_verbatim_span: Introduce controlled modifications to the algorithm (e.g., swapping ads between users or changing content delivery methods).
llm_justification: This describes a verification/validation method (controlled experimentation) to assess consistent performance across different configurations, which is the core concern of Reliability, Fall-back and Reproducibility rather than general safety hazards (4) or ongoing monitoring (23).

component_description: Access rights are issued to users and administrators upon approval by an authorised officer
llm_verbatim_span: Access rights are issued to users and administrators upon approval by an authorised officer
llm_justification: This is a specific security/access-control requirement (who may grant access rights), which the codebook explicitly assigns to Resilience to Attack and Security (3) rather than broader risk management or data governance.

component_description: Consider implementing feedback channels and decision review channels
llm_verbatim_span: Consider implementing feedback channels and decision review channels
llm_justification: This is Risk Management (19) rather than Stakeholder Participation (14) because the emphasis is on establishing formal channels for review and redress of decisions (accountability mechanisms), not on incorporating stakeholders into the design/development process itself.

component_description: 23. Have we taken into account users in the enterprise who have disabilities and how this group can take part in  the benefits of using AI, and if so, whether adaptations are necessary?
llm_verbatim_span: users in the enterprise who have disabilities and how this group can take part in  the benefits of using AI, and if so, whether adaptations are necessary
llm_justification: This component directly addresses ensuring the system serves users with disabilities through necessary adaptations, which is the core concern of Accessibility and Unfair Design (13), not discriminatory outcomes from algorithmic decisions (12).

component_description: Could the system have a big impact on decisions regarding the right to life?
human_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)
llm_verbatim_span: Could the system have a big impact on decisions regarding the right to life?
llm_justification: This question directly assesses the AI system's impact on a fundamental right (right to life), which falls under Privacy (7)'s scope of evaluating impact on physical, mental and/or moral integrity and fundamental rights, rather than General Safety (4) which focuses on technical hazard identification or Risk Management (19) which concerns governance processes.

component_description: PC-02 Documentation: Requires structured documentation of system robustness, covering development, deployment, operation, maintenance, roles, responsibilities, and version control.
llm_verbatim_span: Requires structured documentation of system robustness, covering development, deployment, operation, maintenance, roles, responsibilities, and version control.
llm_justification: The requirement for structured documentation covering development, deployment, operation, maintenance, and version control directly maps to Traceability (9), which concerns documenting the development process to enable tracking of data, models, and decisions, rather than Auditability (18) which is about the broader capability for independent evaluation.

component_description: start an Audit Journal that collects relevant information on interactions and exchanges of information with the client, important decisions taken, problems detected, suggestions for improvement for the present or future, etc
llm_verbatim_span: start an Audit Journal that collects relevant information on interactions and exchanges of information with the client, important decisions taken, problems detected, suggestions for improvement
llm_justification: This is about documenting the audit process itself (client interactions, audit decisions, findings) rather than documenting the AI system's development (code 9) or enabling the system to be audited (code 18); it fits Auditing Context (25) which covers audit-specific governance including evidence strategy and traceable linkage from findings to actions.

component_description: How are the results of all risk assessment, risk management and risk control procedures in relation to safety and reliability of the AI System factored into necessary or desirable alterations of (the design of) the AI System? How is this process documented?
llm_verbatim_span: How are the results of all risk assessment, risk management and risk control procedures in relation to safety and reliability of the AI System factored into necessary or desirable alterations of (the design of) the AI System?
llm_justification: This focuses on how risk findings drive system alterations to maintain reliability and safety over time, which is the core concern of Reliability, Fall-back and Reproducibility (6) - managing system performance consistency and adaptation. While it mentions risk management, the dominant requirement is about the feedback loop that ensures continued reliable performance through design changes, not the risk governance process itself (19) or safety hazard identification (4).

component_description: What does the model assume about the data?
llm_verbatim_span: What does the model assume about the data?
llm_justification: This asks about data quality requirements and assumptions underlying the model's predictions, which is central to ensuring appropriate precision and performance—the core concern of Accuracy (5)—rather than data provenance/logging (9), compliance practices (8), or reliability over time (6).

component_description: What elements of the training and development “supply chain” have been outsourced? If handed off to a third party, are their services subject to the same levels of quality control as the Organisation?
human_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)
llm_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)
llm_verbatim_span: What elements of the training and development "supply chain" have been outsourced? If handed off to a third party, are their services subject to the same levels of quality control as the Organisation?
llm_justification: This explicitly asks about outsourced elements of the supply chain and whether third-party services meet equivalent quality standards, which is the core concern of Third-party Risks (27) regarding vendor assurance and residual risk, rather than general Risk Management (19) or Auditability (18).

component_description: Model selection and training
llm_verbatim_span: Model selection and training
llm_justification: This is a short category label naming a development-phase engineering activity; code 22 (System Design and Development) captures structured engineering practices that reduce defects before deployment, which includes model selection and training processes, rather than post-deployment monitoring (23) or outcome metrics like accuracy (5).

component_description: Ensure that ethics, bias, social, and legal aspects are included in the strategy.
human_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)
llm_verbatim_span: Ensure that ethics, bias, social, and legal aspects are included in the strategy.
llm_justification: This is Risk Management (19) rather than Organisational Context (20) because it prescribes the PROCESS of incorporating multiple risk dimensions (ethics, bias, social, legal) into strategic planning, which is the essence of risk governance, not merely stating business purpose or alignment.

component_description: Are the characteristics of data used to train the AI component identified, documented and duly justified?
llm_verbatim_span: Are the characteristics of data used to train the AI component identified, documented and duly justified?
llm_justification: This asks for identification and documentation of training data characteristics (provenance/source), which is explicitly covered by Traceability (9) as tracking data in the development process, not data-protection compliance (8) or data quality/suitability (5).

component_description: Conduct pilot studies
llm_verbatim_span: Conduct pilot studies
llm_justification: Pilot studies are a pre-deployment design and validation practice that tests system behavior in controlled conditions to reduce defects, distinguishing this from post-deployment monitoring (23) or reliability outcomes (6).

component_description: Is this AI System an expansion of a previous activity? If yes, determine whether a previous assessment has been done. If a previous assessment has been done, what has changed in this data activity and why (refer to previous assessment)?
llm_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)
llm_verbatim_span: Is this AI System an expansion of a previous activity? If yes, determine whether a previous assessment has been done.
llm_justification: This asks about the system's relationship to prior organizational activities and assessments, establishing context about whether this is a new or evolved deployment—core to understanding organizational context and strategy rather than traceability of technical outputs or risk management processes.

component_description: What types of data are collected (personal, non-personal, special categories)?
llm_verbatim_span: What types of data are collected (personal, non-personal, special categories)?
llm_justification: This is Data Governance (8) rather than Traceability (9) because it asks about data classification for compliance purposes (personal vs. special categories under data protection law), not about data provenance or sourcing; it's also not Privacy (7) because it focuses on the compliance practice of categorizing data types rather than assessing rights/risk impact on data subjects.

component_description: rains:Limitation and Risks. Extends sao:InformationElement to describe: Known or anticipated limitations of datasets, models, or infrastructure. Risks such as biases, incorrect use cases, or compliance challenges.
llm_verbatim_span: Known or anticipated limitations of datasets, models, or infrastructure. Risks such as biases, incorrect use cases, or compliance challenges.
llm_justification: This is Risk Management (19) rather than General Safety (4) or Avoidance of Unfair Bias (12) because it establishes a broad process for identifying and documenting multiple types of adverse impacts (biases, misuse, compliance issues) rather than focusing on a specific safety hazard or bias mitigation technique.

component_description: Is the impact of the use of the algorithm clear to data subjects?
llm_verbatim_span: Is the impact of the use of the algorithm clear to data subjects?
llm_justification: This asks whether the system's impact is communicated clearly to data subjects (users), which is Communication (11) rather than Explainability (10) which focuses on reasoning/how conclusions are reached, or Privacy (7) which focuses on rights/risk assessment rather than clarity of communication.

component_description: In the case of military or lethal uses of the AI System: (a) Is the AI System fully autonomous? (b) Is there a shutdown function triggered by designated personnel? (c) Is there effective human oversight in place?
llm_verbatim_span: Is there a shutdown function triggered by designated personnel? (c) Is there effective human oversight in place?
llm_justification: While question (a) touches on autonomy (code 1), questions (b) and (c) directly address Human Oversight mechanisms: shutdown/override capability and human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop governance, which are the defining features of code 2 rather than the user-facing autonomy effects of code 1.

component_description: Organisations may also wish to centralise such information digitally in a process log. This would enable the organisation to make available, in one place, information that may assist in demonstrating to concerned parties and affected decision subjects both the responsibility of design and practices and the justifiability of the outcomes of your system’s processing behaviour.
llm_verbatim_span: enable the organisation to make available, in one place, information that may assist in demonstrating to concerned parties and affected decision subjects both the responsibility of design and practices and the justifiability of the outcomes
llm_justification: The dominant requirement is enabling independent evaluation and demonstration of the system's design responsibility and outcome justifiability to external parties, which is the core definition of Auditability (18), rather than merely internal traceability (9) or general risk documentation (19).

component_description: Sector-Specific AI Solutions: Promote AI in key Italian industries, ensuring solutions are adapted to specific needs, such as product quality and regulatory compliance.
llm_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)
llm_verbatim_span: Promote AI in key Italian industries, ensuring solutions are adapted to specific needs, such as product quality and regulatory compliance.
llm_justification: This is a strategic directive about AI adoption and alignment to business/sectoral purpose and requirements (product quality, compliance), which is the core of Organisational Context and Strategy, rather than a specific technical requirement or compliance mapping (21).

component_description: What residual risk still persists and needs to be catered for?
llm_verbatim_span: What residual risk still persists and needs to be catered for?
llm_justification: This explicitly asks about residual risk identification and management, which is the core concern of Risk Management (19) rather than a specific safety hazard (4), security threat (3), or third-party dependency (27).

component_description: Conduct audits regularly to assess model risk effectiveness, taking feedback from internal and external sources to align with your AI maturity.
llm_verbatim_span: Conduct audits regularly to assess model risk effectiveness, taking feedback from internal and external sources
llm_justification: The dominant requirement is to conduct audits for independent evaluation of model risk effectiveness with internal and external feedback, which is the core definition of Auditability (18), rather than Risk Management (19) which would focus on the risk identification/mitigation process itself rather than the audit mechanism.

component_description: Are the algorithms state of the art?
llm_verbatim_span: Are the algorithms state of the art?
llm_justification: This question concerns whether appropriate engineering practices and design choices were made during system development (selecting state-of-the-art algorithms), which is a design-time quality control rather than a post-deployment performance metric or specific safety hazard assessment.

component_description: review of datasets
llm_verbatim_span: review of datasets
llm_justification: This is about examining and documenting which datasets were used (data provenance and tracking), which is the core concern of Traceability (9), rather than data quality/suitability (5), data protection compliance (8), or accuracy outcomes (5).

component_description: Is there a recourse process established for clients that wish to challenge the decision?
llm_verbatim_span: Is there a recourse process established for clients that wish to challenge the decision?
llm_justification: This explicitly asks about redress procedures for affected individuals, which is a defining element of Risk Management (19) rather than Auditability (18) which concerns independent evaluation capability, or Human Oversight (2) which concerns operational intervention mechanisms.

component_description: What measures would be taken to avoid automation bias or anchoring to the AI System?
llm_verbatim_span: avoid automation bias or anchoring to the AI System
llm_justification: The component explicitly names automation bias and anchoring, which are specific forms of over-reliance on AI that affect human decision-making and behavior—the core concern of Human Agency and Autonomy (1) rather than Human Oversight (2) which focuses on intervention mechanisms.

component_description: Identify risks that threaten AI strategic goals and objectives.
llm_verbatim_span: Identify risks that threaten AI strategic goals and objectives.
llm_justification: This is Risk Management (19) rather than General Safety (4) because it concerns the broader governance process of identifying risks to strategic goals, not safety-specific hazards or consequences of system failure.

component_description: Job changes and terminations of employment are monitored for adjustment of access rights and for revocation of means of identity and authentication
llm_verbatim_span: Job changes and terminations of employment are monitored for adjustment of access rights and for revocation of means of identity and authentication
llm_justification: This is a specific security/access-control concern (revoking access when staff leave, adjusting rights on role changes) which the codebook explicitly lists under Resilience to Attack and Security (3), not broader risk management.

component_description: Lay out an approach to manage AI risks and report to stakeholders for transparency
llm_verbatim_span: Lay out an approach to manage AI risks and report to stakeholders for transparency
llm_justification: The dominant requirement is establishing a risk management process with stakeholder reporting, which is the defining characteristic of Risk Management (19), not merely documentation for audit (18) or communication of system capabilities (11).

component_description: the known or expected risks, including biases, associated with models
llm_verbatim_span: the known or expected risks, including biases, associated with models
llm_justification: The explicit mention of "biases" as a specific risk category points to Avoidance of Unfair Bias (12) rather than general Risk Management (19), which would address risks broadly without this discriminatory-outcome focus.

component_description: Could our AI system have an adverse impact on the environment?
llm_verbatim_span: Could our AI system have an adverse impact on the environment?
llm_justification: This is a direct question about environmental impact of the AI system, which is the core concern of Environmental Well-being (15), not a broader risk management process (19) or any other principle.

component_description: Identify Unsafe Control Actions (UCAs): For each control action, define situations where it could be hazardous (e.g., an automated braking system might trigger in safe conditions, leading to a rear-end collision).
llm_verbatim_span: Identify Unsafe Control Actions (UCAs): For each control action, define situations where it could be hazardous
llm_justification: This describes a structured engineering practice (UCA identification, a core STPA technique) performed during design to reduce unsafe behavior before deployment, which is the defining characteristic of System Design and Development (22), rather than General Safety (4) which focuses on broader risk identification/mitigation or Reliability (6) which concerns consistent performance.

llm_verbatim_span: Privacy impact assesment in best case
llm_justification: The component prescribes a privacy impact assessment (a data protection compliance practice) for processing personal/confidential data, which is the core definition of Data Governance (8), not Privacy (7) which focuses on rights/risk impact to data subjects.

component_description: Have appropriate precautions been taken, such as systematic control by a human operator which could then be reduced in the production phase?
llm_verbatim_span: systematic control by a human operator which could then be reduced in the production phase
llm_justification: The component directly addresses governance mechanisms for human intervention and the appropriate level of human control (human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop) at different lifecycle stages, which is the core concern of Human Oversight (2) rather than the broader risk-management process (19).

component_description: Is community feedback on the algorithms encouraged and taken into account?
llm_verbatim_span: Is community feedback on the algorithms encouraged and taken into account?
llm_justification: This directly asks about incorporating feedback from affected parties (community) into the system, which is the defining characteristic of Stakeholder Participation (14), rather than Communication (11) which focuses on conveying information TO users rather than receiving input FROM them.

llm_verbatim_span: What is the Organisation's lawful basis for processing personal information? What measures does the Organisation take to ensure compliance?

llm_verbatim_span: The specific task, and methods used to implement the task, that the AI system will support is defined

component_description: Does the AI System raise risks of psychological and behavioral manipulation, coercion, or excessive nudging?
human_principle: Context-Driven Alignment (inductively derived; not in original ALTAI)
llm_verbatim_span: Does the AI System raise risks of psychological and behavioral manipulation, coercion, or excessive nudging?

llm_verbatim_span: Is the traceability of the systemcomposition (including soft- and hardwarecomposition and components) guaranteed?

llm_verbatim_span: Will the system interface with other IT systems?

llm_verbatim_span: who is accountable for the creation of various specifications including the dataset

llm_verbatim_span: AI infringing on break times, impacting worker health and productivity

llm_verbatim_span: Describe potential outcomes if a hazard materializes (e.g., "Misclassification of medical images could lead to incorrect treatments")

llm_verbatim_span: Measurable continuous improvement activities are integrated into system updates and include regular stakeholder engagement.

component_description: Is the data high quality data?
